title: the harbor map's component keys and source pointers are posix on every box
intention: register.py names a component and a source pointer with forward slashes on every host, so a component matches the owning_component a ticket spells and a prose-standing finding names tools/fx_widget, not tools\fx_widget.
why: On Windows, str(d.relative_to(cairn_root)) (register.py:100, _component_key) and str(path.relative_to(_SRC_ROOT)) (:69, _rel) give backslashes, so the map's grouping key never equals a ticket's owning_component and test_the_map_wears_the_one_label's test_fixture_prose_standing_is_a_finding_not_a_status reds. Found answering ad6f3d0b265c's FIXME.
traces_to: Law 8 (the harbor map's proofs hold on every box the fleet runs); outline: the map wears the one label (ticket ad6f3d0b265c).
how: .as_posix() in place of str(...) at both lines; a host-independent tooth feeds PureWindowsPath inputs so the red-first reading holds on Linux too.

clauses.claim: _component_key and _rel give posix keys and pointers for PureWindowsPath inputs on every host (test_a_windows_path_keys_and_points_posix_on_every_host): red with str(), green with .as_posix(); on Windows test_fixture_prose_standing_is_a_finding_not_a_status reds without the change and greens with it

decisions.text: D1: both lines in register.py (_rel :69, _component_key :100) use .as_posix(); nothing else changes.
D2: the host-independent tooth test_a_windows_path_keys_and_points_posix_on_every_host, _SRC_ROOT swapped and restored in a finally; PROVES['f1d1ebc0c4d0']['1'] names it.

out: the harbor map's other keys and views
